vacuous_run_gate_class.finding: MANDATORY for every -run-shaped acceptance criterion. `go test -run <selector>` EXITS 0 when the selector matches NOTHING.
vacuous_run_gate_class.measured_negative: go test ./internal/eval -run 'TestZzNoSuchTestIter252' -count=1 -v -> rc=0, 0 '=== RUN' lines, 'ok ... [no tests to run]'
vacuous_run_gate_class.measured_positive: go test ./internal/eval -run '^TestTaggedValue$' -count=1 -v -> rc=0, 5 '=== RUN' lines (1 top-level + 4 subtests)
vacuous_run_gate_class.measured_partial: go test ./internal/eval -run '^(TestTaggedValue|TestZzNope252)$' -> rc=0, top-level count 1, expected 2. Only a COUNT assertion catches an orphaned selector name.
vacuous_run_gate_class.consequence: The exit codes are IDENTICAL. Any criterion shaped 'go test -run A|B passes' is green BEFORE either test is written and stays green if a rename orphans the selector. V1 carries 54 such floor-less invocations across 16 files in design_docs/planned; this design doc has ZERO and this plan introduces ZERO.
vacuous_run_gate_class.mandatory_floor: go test <pkg> -run '<sel>' -count=1 -v > $LOG 2>&1; RC=$?; N=$(grep -c '^=== RUN   Test[^/]*$' $LOG); [ $N -eq 0 ] && { echo 'INSTRUMENT FAILURE: selector matched NO tests'; exit 3; }; [ $N -ne <EXPECTED_N> ] && { echo "INSTRUMENT FAILURE: expected <EXPECTED_N>, ran $N"; exit 3; }; [ $RC -eq 0 ] || exit 1
vacuous_run_gate_class.regex_note: '^=== RUN   Test[^/]*$' counts TOP-LEVEL tests only; subtests are '=== RUN   TestX/sub' and also start at column 0, so the [^/]*$ anchor is load-bearing. N==0 is an INSTRUMENT FAILURE (exit 3), never a pass.

baseline_ratchet_failure_modes.merge_conflict: Exact-match means ANY count-touching PR regenerates baseline.json, so concurrent worktrees will conflict. Deterministic key ordering + one-key-per-line JSON keeps conflicts textual and small, and `make listrep-baseline` regenerates in one command. A conflict resolved by PICKING ONE SIDE is a silent baseline forgery - so the gate re-runs after any baseline merge and exact-match catches a mis-resolved file immediately. That is precisely the property exact-match buys over 'may only decrease'.
baseline_ratchet_failure_modes.can_a_stale_baseline_hide_a_new_violatio: Rule 1: NO. Exact-match reds on drift in either direction, including a package silently vanishing (DEFECT-9's MISSING_PACKAGE class, which the doc did not specify and this plan adds). Rule 2: NOT APPLICABLE - it is never ratcheted; any diagnostic fails unconditionally, so no baseline can hide it. THE RESIDUAL IS THE ENUMERATOR, NOT THE RATCHET: a site the scan cannot SEE (build tag, nested module, dot-dir) is not in the baseline and never will be - which is why the blind spots are a PRINTED baseline field and a listrep -help section, not a footnote.
